newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-UNDERDOG ROLE COULD HELP PATRIOTS - PARCELLS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-UNDERDOG ROLE COULD HELP PATRIOTS - PARCELLS.

text.p: New England Patriots coach Bill Parcells said Friday his team's status as 14-point underdogs for Super Bowl XXXI has helped to further focus his players on the difficult task of beating the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.

"I think it makes the team fully aware that they are going to be challenged or that the majority of people think they are going to be challenged on a very high level," Parcells said in his final news conference before the big game.

"If the underdog role serves you well, it's in the ability of the coach to point out what the public perception is ... and it makes your team aware of the fact that everyone thinks they're going to have to play very well to win.
"It kind of gets their attention and makes them focus on 'hey we're going to have to be on top of our game' and that's really what you want as a coach. You want them to feel challenged and alert."
Parcells was not the least bit surprised that the Packers feel it is their turn to win the title after getting to the NFC championship game last season, a year in which New England went 6-10.
"I don't think going into the season that very many people expected us to be here right this moment," Parcells said with pride.
He characterised his team as "a very unified, spunky, high-quality person team. They're good kids...and it's not hard to coach them at all."
And while he is known for innovative game plans and meticulous preparation, Parcells knows that even the best laid plans can go awry in a hurry.
"Any coach will tell you, right at the beginning of the game, there's always something happens that surprises you," he addmitted.
In a light-hearted session, Parcells once again deflected questions about widespread reports that he would leave the Patriots following Sunday's game to take conrol of the New York Jets.
"It's been a lot of fun coaching this team, but I don't have a crystal ball," Parcells said.
"I honestly at this moment do not know what's going to occur. But I think the time to wait is growing narrow and we'll find out at some point."
Parcells will meet with Patriots owner Robert Kraft after the game to settle the question of his future.
But he did take a moment for some serious reflection on his coaching life.

"I'm happy that I had the opportunity to be in this league and that this sport of football has allowed me to raise my family and put three wonderful daughters into productive roles in society, and I am very grateful for that," Parcells said.
"I'm happy that I have had this opportunity, and if it does end soon or next week or next year I'm still going out way ahead.
"If it continues on, it's icing on the cake."
